Prime Minister Narendra Modi with his Poland counterpart Donald Tusk during a meeting in New Delhi on October 22, 2026 | Photo Credit: Sushil Kumar Verma
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday (October 22, 2026) met the Poland Prime Minister Donald Tusk in New Delhi.
The Polish PM Donald Tusk is on a three-day visit to India amid renewed global push to end the conflict in Ukraine.
After meeting Mr. Tusk, Mr. Modi said “We have decided to take a series of measure to enhance India-Poland strategic cooperation.”
After the talks, the Prime Minister said “We have agreed to boost cooperation in areas of defence, space and nuclear energy.”
Mr. Modi said “India-European Union free trade agreement will further broaden economic engagement between India and Poland.”
The Prime Minister said “Our growing economic strength has created new opportunities for India-Poland partnership. India and Poland believe in democratic values, rule of law.”
Mr. Modi said “Be it Ukraine or West Asia, India will continue to support every meaningful effort towards peace”.
